fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Winter, Ideas and the Seasonal Mind", "body": "Joakim describes life near the Arctic, where summer brings almost endless daylight and long winters once kept households indoors. He hears the Swedish word for idea in the old word for winter hibernation, so that ideas are gathered in the cold months and brought forth in summer. Chance extends the image, reading hibernation as dreaming and summer as planting those dreams in action. Joakim then argues that climate shapes culture, contrasting northern lives built around storing food with the looser rhythms he sees in warmer lands, a broad generalization the two explore together."}, {"title": "The Bock Saga and Its Ancient Tongues", "body": "Chance invites Joakim to introduce the Bock Saga, which Joakim presents as an oral mythology brought forward by Ior Bock and told in Finnish, Swedish and English. Joakim says the saga holds that English is around ten thousand years old, formed from the Aser and Vaner languages, with Swedish keeping the older root tongue and Finnish carrying the other. These are the saga's claims as Joakim relays them, and he adds that the Germanic family plainly shares a common root. Chance offers his own view that English was cobbled together later for a servant class."}, {"title": "Dead Languages and Legal Control", "body": "Chance argues that Latin, called a dead language, survives mainly through the Vatican, and that legalese is Latin kept fixed so that definitions stay under the control of those who write the law, letting a decree from a century ago mean the same today. Joakim agrees, calling Latin and Russian made-up languages in his view and saying the church held a monopoly over reading and writing, with ordinary people at risk for learning it. These are the speakers' interpretations rather than established history."}, {"title": "Gustav Vasa, Templars and Military Ranks", "body": "Joakim tells how Sweden's break from Rome under Gustav Vasa, which he thinks may have been planned for generations, moved church taxes into state hands and spread reading through propaganda and the Protestant movement. He says the saga ties the Vasa kings to a sideline of the Bock family and calls Vasa a Templar. Joakim credits Gustav Adolf with pioneering modern warfare, and argues that military ranks such as captain and lieutenant carry a pagan counting of tens, while Chance adds the Latin root of decimate."}, {"title": "Hidden Orders, Architecture and the Finnish Temple", "body": "Chance questions the official histories of old cathedrals and universities, citing Harvard and arguing that its grand architecture appeared before any need for it. Joakim, turning to fraternal orders, says the Hospitallers and Templars were Jarl families who went underground when the church took Sweden and Finland, aiming to preserve pagan memory, though he calls parts of this speculation. He then describes a long effort by saga followers to reach what they believe is a temple in Finland, now awaiting funding, a foundation to receive donations, and a drilled camera."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Joakim Häggström is a leading researcher on the Bock Saga and occult linguistic history. In his second appearance on InnerVerse, we discuss how dead languages fuel the NWO power structure, the Swedish king Gustav the 1st, pagan connections to military traditions, Templars and other secret societies, and much more.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Tea, Fresh Leaves and Mahala", "body": "Joakim recommends brewing tea from fresh leaves at a gentle heat, never boiling, and lifting them out once they sink, which he says is how tea was made in the old days. He relays that the Bock Saga makes tea central and names the life power drawn from leaves mahala, the first stage in the life force chain, derived from the sun. He separates thin, translucent leaves that suit tea from thicker leaves with fluid inside, and Chance compares mahala to prana or chi. The health benefits are Joakim's own recommendations, not established claims."}, {"title": "The Double-Headed Eagle and the Dragon", "body": "Asked about the double-headed eagle, Joakim reads it as the two heads of the Templar order and speculates that the last such heads were the Russian Romanovs and a second royal house of England, guessing at titles of world master and grandmaster, while Chance frames the Bolshevik Revolution as an engineered plundering. Turning to Saint George, Joakim calls the dragon tale propaganda against pagans and links the dragon to the Midgard serpent and the ouroboros, a word Chance parses etymologically. Both stress that word origins remain uncertain."}, {"title": "The Sun, the Temple and Sacred Sexuality", "body": "Joakim calls the Finnish temple the pinnacle of the ouroboros system and a headquarters of the pagan world, and describes the saga's Udin, the sun, as the all-creator with five elements. He says that in this story human beings carry a spark of the sun, and that sexuality matters as much as the brain, which he contrasts with taboos in the Abrahamic religions. Chance links cathedral fertility statues and repression to diminished thinking. Joakim adds that he cannot imagine the world becoming pagan again but thinks we can mimic it."}, {"title": "East, Hermes and the Danger of Interpretation", "body": "Chance asks whether the saga connects to Eastern wisdom such as Lao Tzu and the Yi Ching, and Joakim answers that he knows of Silk Road trade but not of any saga link. Chance proposes that Odin, Hermes and Thoth overlap, and says several trusted acquaintances reported visionary contact with that figure. Joakim keeps the saga to basics, warns that adding personal material costs its purity, and calls destiny a trickster. Both agree interpretation is risky and may be bent by films and thought forms."}, {"title": "Soul, Spirit and Burial Traditions", "body": "Joakim says the saga separates spirit, carried in the breath, from soul, held in the body's structure, which he links to cremation with ashes placed under a tree. Chance speculates that preserved bodies and relics might leave psychic echoes and calls church customs necromantic, a view he offers as speculation. Joakim notes skull and bone symbolism in an old Stockholm church and says a cross bearing a dead figure inverts a heathen symbol of a best friend. Chance adds that the Vatican works like a corporation claiming authority through Christ's office."}]

fields.Plus Quotes JSON: [{"text": "I'd say I never really can imagine the world to become like pagan ever. But at least we can try to have some kind of mimics.", "author": "Joakim Häggström", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/21f1d3d8-55b9-43c9-984d-6d1b7637fe6f/JOCKE-HAGGSTROM.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The further you dig through the layers of occulted information, the more likely you are to run into the most original archetypes that exist, which is the male and female reproductive organs.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "The beautiful thing about the Bock Saga is also that it tells that all humans on this planet come from the same source, or the same people.", "author": "Joakim Häggström", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/21f1d3d8-55b9-43c9-984d-6d1b7637fe6f/JOCKE-HAGGSTROM.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "There are Eastern traditions stemming out of the wisdom of Lao Tzu and Yi Ching, things that just seem to emerge on the scene out of nowhere.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Imagine how little essence there is in those kind of packaged food.", "author": "Joakim Häggström", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/21f1d3d8-55b9-43c9-984d-6d1b7637fe6f/JOCKE-HAGGSTROM.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The mahala comes from the sun. So it's all about sun power.", "author": "Joakim Häggström", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/21f1d3d8-55b9-43c9-984d-6d1b7637fe6f/JOCKE-HAGGSTROM.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "There's a huge amount of overlap in the symbolism between Odin and Hermes or Mercury.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Before I found out about the Bock Saga, I was like really in the wilderness and I didn't know where to go, because there wasn't more information about the Norse mythology at all.", "author": "Joakim Häggström", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/21f1d3d8-55b9-43c9-984d-6d1b7637fe6f/JOCKE-HAGGSTROM.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Interpretation's dangerous, man. It's really like just keeping it to the raw experience and not trying to put too much other adornment on it is probably helpful.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "If you look at it through the Bock Saga, they talk about the soul and the spirit, they are two different things when we die. The spirit goes away in the breath.", "author": "Joakim Häggström", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/21f1d3d8-55b9-43c9-984d-6d1b7637fe6f/JOCKE-HAGGSTROM.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}]
fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "It's interesting if you have this kind of perspective of nature and the cycles, how to use them, and it's sort of baked into the words also, the old words, how we used to live.", "author": "Joakim Häggström", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/21f1d3d8-55b9-43c9-984d-6d1b7637fe6f/JOCKE-HAGGSTROM.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "When you talk about hibernation, that's like dreaming and having your dreams. And then in the waking life, which would be the metaphor of summer, you put them into action, you plant those seeds.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "The military ranks are ranks from within the pagan world system, and the costumes and everything is based on the heathen traditions.", "author": "Joakim Häggström", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/21f1d3d8-55b9-43c9-984d-6d1b7637fe6f/JOCKE-HAGGSTROM.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "David Whitehead says all the time, if you think the fake news is bad, how is the history? It's probably even more fake.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "As I see it, it's those Jarl families, the Earl families, that went underground when the church took over the last part of Europe that was Finland and Sweden.", "author": "Joakim Häggström", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/21f1d3d8-55b9-43c9-984d-6d1b7637fe6f/JOCKE-HAGGSTROM.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "It's never been a better time to open up our minds and dump out all the stuff handed to us by the state and by the church and come in with a blank slate.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "It's better to be like a child and start from the beginning. Sometimes that could be a nice attitude because if you bring all your luggage with you, maybe you miss something.", "author": "Joakim Häggström", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/21f1d3d8-55b9-43c9-984d-6d1b7637fe6f/JOCKE-HAGGSTROM.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "That's the funny thing about routines. When you're in them, time goes quicker and you're doing the same thing over and over again.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}]
